programme.displayName: S3 Buckets: Versioning, Public Access Protection, and Lifecycle Management
programme.subtitle: An SAA-C03-focused Amazon S3 general purpose bucket lab in Europe (London)
programme.description: Create a private Amazon S3 general purpose bucket in eu-west-2, confirm Block Public Access, enable versioning, upload two harmless versions of one test object, and apply a lifecycle rule that permanently deletes noncurrent versions after 30 days. This lab practices SAA-C03 concepts around S3 durability, version recovery, public-access controls, and lifecycle management.
programme.learningOutcome: Explain and configure the S3 controls commonly tested in SAA-C03 scenarios: Block Public Access, S3 Versioning, object-version inspection, and noncurrent-version lifecycle expiration.

tasks.title: Create a private general purpose bucket
tasks.feature: General purpose bucket creation and S3 Block Public Access
tasks.goal: Create exactly one lab bucket named saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> in eu-west-2 with Bucket owner enforced and all four Block Public Access settings enabled.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 scenarios often require selecting an S3 design that prevents accidental public exposure while retaining the default modern object-ownership model. General purpose bucket names must be globally unique, so the unique suffix is genuinely required.

consoleSteps.title: Open Amazon S3
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Amazon S3 console opens.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab Region
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console is scoped to the Region used for this lab.
consoleSteps.warning: A bucket's Region cannot be changed after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Open general purpose buckets
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The General purpose buckets list appears.

consoleSteps.title: Start bucket creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Create bucket page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Set the test bucket name
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket name is accepted when its suffix makes it globally unique.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put personal, customer, or confidential information in a bucket name.

consoleSteps.title: Keep ACLs disabled
consoleSteps.expectedResult: ACLs remain disabled for the new bucket.

consoleSteps.title: Keep public access blocked
consoleSteps.instruction: Keep all four Block Public Access settings enabled.

instructions.text: Keep all four Block Public Access settings enabled.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The new bucket is configured with all four bucket-level Block Public Access settings enabled.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not disable Block Public Access for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Create the bucket
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The new general purpose bucket appears in the bucket list.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the same general purpose bucket. Replace <unique-suffix> with a lowercase, non-confidential value that makes the name globally unique; use that exact resulting bucket name in every later command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Amazon S3 creates the bucket in eu-west-2.
cliSteps.warning: For Regions other than us-east-1, the create-bucket command requires a matching LocationConstraint.

verification.title: Confirm bucket-level public access protection
verification.instruction: Run `aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> --region eu-west-2`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/get-public-access-block.html
verification.expectedResult: The returned PublicAccessBlockConfiguration shows BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, and RestrictPublicBuckets as true.

tasks.title: Enable and verify S3 Versioning
tasks.goal: Enable versioning on the lab bucket before uploading the test object.
tasks.whyItMatters: Versioning keeps multiple variants of the same object key and supports recovery from unintended overwrites or deletes. It is also the prerequisite for lifecycle actions that manage noncurrent object versions.

consoleSteps.title: Open the lab bucket
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket details page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the exact bucket created in Task 1.

consoleSteps.title: Open bucket properties
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket Properties tab opens.

consoleSteps.title: Edit versioning
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Bucket Versioning edit page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Enable versioning
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Versioning is selected for the bucket.

consoleSteps.title: Save the versioning change
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket reports that versioning is enabled.
consoleSteps.warning: AWS documents that first-time versioning enablement can take time to propagate and recommends waiting 15 minutes before PUT or DELETE operations.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket created in Task 1.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command sets the bucket versioning state to Enabled.
cliSteps.warning: Wait 15 minutes before the Task 3 upload commands because AWS documents possible intermittent NoSuchKey errors while first-time versioning enablement propagates.

verification.title: Confirm the versioning state
verification.instruction: Run `aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> --region eu-west-2`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/developerguide/s3_example_s3_GetBucketVersioning_section.html
verification.expectedResult: The response contains `Status` with the value `Enabled`.

tasks.title: Create two object versions and a lifecycle rule
tasks.feature: Object versions and S3 Lifecycle noncurrent-version expiration
tasks.goal: Upload two harmless revisions of lab/versioning-test.txt and configure a lifecycle rule named saa-c03-expire-noncurrent-versions that permanently deletes noncurrent versions under the lab/ prefix after 30 days.
tasks.whyItMatters: This is a core SAA-C03 tradeoff: versioning improves recovery, but retained noncurrent versions can continue to consume storage. A lifecycle rule can control the retention period for those older versions.

consoleSteps.title: Open the Objects tab
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket Objects view opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Before uploading, create a harmless local text file named saa-c03-versioning-test.txt containing only `SAA-C03 sample version one`.

consoleSteps.title: Start the first upload
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Upload page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Choose the first test file
consoleSteps.expectedResult: A local file picker opens.

consoleSteps.title: Upload the first version
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The upload status page reports a successful upload.

consoleSteps.title: Change the local sample text
consoleSteps.instruction: Replace the local file content with `SAA-C03 sample version two`.

instructions.text: Replace the local file content with `SAA-C03 sample version two`.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The same local filename now contains harmless revised test data.
consoleSteps.warning: Keep the same filename so that the second upload uses the same S3 object key.

consoleSteps.title: Start the second upload
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Upload page opens again.

consoleSteps.title: Choose the revised test file
consoleSteps.expectedResult: A local file picker opens.

consoleSteps.title: Upload the second version
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The upload status page reports a successful upload.
consoleSteps.warning: Uploading an object with an existing key to a versioning-enabled bucket creates another object version.

cliSteps.explanation: Upload the first version. This command depends on a manually created local file named saa-c03-versioning-test.txt containing only `SAA-C03 sample version one`.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local file is uploaded at the lab/versioning-test.txt key.
cliSteps.warning: Run this only after the 15-minute versioning-propagation wait described in Task 2.

cliSteps.explanation: After manually changing the same local file to contain only `SAA-C03 sample version two`, upload it to the identical S3 key to create a second object version.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Amazon S3 creates a new version of lab/versioning-test.txt and retains the prior version as noncurrent.
cliSteps.warning: Do not change the destination key between the two uploads.

cliSteps.explanation: Create one lifecycle rule that applies only to objects whose keys begin with lab/ and requests permanent deletion of noncurrent versions after 30 days.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The lifecycle configuration is set on the bucket.
cliSteps.warning: Putting a lifecycle configuration replaces the bucket's existing lifecycle configuration. Use this only on the dedicated lab bucket.

cliSteps.explanation: Retrieve the lifecycle configuration after creating it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes the saa-c03-expire-noncurrent-versions rule with the lab/ filter and a 30-day NoncurrentVersionExpiration setting.

verification.title: Inspect the two object versions
verification.instruction: Run `aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket saa-c03-s3-lab-<unique-suffix> --prefix lab/versioning-test.txt --region eu-west-2`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/list-object-versions.html
verification.expectedResult: The response lists version metadata for the lab/versioning-test.txt key and identifies whether each returned version is latest.

verification.title: Confirm the lifecycle rule in the console
verification.instruction: Open the Management tab and inspect Lifecycle rules for saa-c03-expire-noncurrent-versions. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/how-to-set-lifecycle-configuration-intro.html
verification.expectedResult: The rule is enabled, limited to the lab/ prefix, and configured to permanently delete noncurrent versions after 30 days.

warnings.cost: Creating a bucket is not charged, but S3 storage and data transfer can incur charges. The lifecycle rule does not remove the noncurrent test version until it becomes eligible after 30 days.
warnings.safety: Do not disable Block Public Access. Do not upload real, personal, customer, regulated, or confidential data. Deleting object versions and deleting the bucket are irreversible.
warnings.credentials: Use an already authenticated AWS Management Console session or an already configured AWS CLI environment. Do not place access keys, secrets, MFA codes, or account identifiers in bucket names, object names, files, or commands.
warnings.region: This follow along uses eu-west-2. The CLI create-bucket command includes LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 because the bucket is not being created in us-east-1.

findings.message: The local text-file preparation and revision are intentionally manual so each listed CLI item remains exactly one AWS CLI command. Confirm that the same local filename is used for both uploads.

AWS recommends waiting 15 minutes after first enabling versioning before issuing PUT or DELETE operations. If the upload commands encounter intermittent NoSuchKey errors, wait and retry them manually.
The console flow can vary slightly by AWS console release. The documented labels used here are General purpose buckets, Properties, Bucket Versioning, Management, and Create lifecycle rule.
